subject: Literature
title: The Future of the Nobel Prize
description: A 60-second lesson on The Future of the Nobel Prize.

hook.text: The Nobel Prize in Literature turns every October into a global debate about what literature is and who it belongs to.

buildup.text: Critics call for more diversity: only seventeen women have won in over a century, and entire regions remain unrepresented.

discovery.text: Some propose expanding the prize to include digital storytelling, graphic novels, and oral performance traditions.

twist.text: Others argue the prize should not change at all, because its conservatism is what gives it enduring authority.

climax.text: The Nobel's future will depend on whether it can honor tradition while reflecting a rapidly changing literary world.

punchline.text: The world's greatest literary prize is still writing its own story.

quiz.question: What criticism is most commonly directed at the Nobel Prize in Literature?
options: The prize money is too low to attract top writers
Only seventeen women have won in over a century, and many regions are unrepresented
Too many prizes are awarded each year
